market_summary: A sharp AI-spending-driven tech selloff hit US markets on Nov 2-3, 2026 (Nasdaq -2.9%, worst day in ~5 months) after Apple's weak margin guidance and Amazon's EPS miss overshadowed otherwise solid revenue numbers; Microsoft was a relative bright spot after beating on Azure/AI strength. In Singapore, the STI is down 1.4% in October with the three major banks (>50% of index weight) under pressure from bond-yield-driven mark-to-market losses ahead of Q3 results due Nov 4-6, UOB seen as least exposed and OCBC most exposed. Breadth is narrow and volatility elevated across both markets; near-term price action will be dominated by the SG bank earnings cluster this week and lingering AI-capex anxiety in US mega-caps.

picks.thesis: Microsoft beat on both lines with strong Azure/AI monetization and a one-off $3.2B Anthropic stake gain, yet the stock has been dragged down with the broader Nasdaq selloff (-2.8% on Nov 2-3) despite fundamentals being the sector's strongest print this earnings season. Analyst coverage is almost unanimously bullish (52 buy/5 hold/0 sell) with ~25% implied upside to consensus target, suggesting the recent pullback is sentiment-driven rather than fundamental.
picks.news: Microsoft beat on top and bottom lines Oct 30 2026 with strong Azure growth and a $3.2B Anthropic stake gain plus lower-than-expected restructuring costs; shares still fell with the broader tech rout on Nov 2-3.
picks.risks: If AI capex concerns persist and investors rotate out of all mega-cap tech indiscriminately regardless of fundamentals, MSFT could keep drifting lower with the index; a weak Azure guide in the next quarter would also undercut the thesis.

picks.thesis: Alphabet is in a severe, accelerating downtrend: -18.8% over 1 month and -26.1% over 3 months, trading 17-18% below both its 50- and 200-day moving averages. A recent analyst downgrade (Citizens, Oct 29) reinforces the negative momentum shift, and the stock is caught in the same AI-capex anxiety hitting the whole sector, with no fresh positive catalyst in the news flow to counter it.
picks.news: Citizens downgraded GOOGL from Market Outperform to Market Perform on Oct 29 2026; broader Nasdaq tumbled 2.9% on Nov 2 amid AI spending concerns pulling down high-multiple tech names.
picks.risks: Stock is already down a lot and could be oversold/due for a bounce; any reassurance on AI capex ROI or a strong cloud/ad number at next earnings could trigger a sharp short squeeze given still-high consensus price targets (45.7% implied upside).

picks.thesis: UOB reports Q3 results Nov 4 and is explicitly flagged as the least exposed of the three Singapore banks to bond-yield-driven mark-to-market losses (small SGD7bn trading book, only SGD50-80m estimated hit), while its stock has already priced in less damage than peers (-6% 1m vs OCBC's -12.5%). This relative resilience combined with a lower beta (0.91) makes it the safer way to play a potential stabilization in SG bank sentiment post-earnings.
picks.news: UOB reports Nov 4 2026; flagged by Minichart (Oct 23) as least exposed to bond-yield-driven MTM losses versus DBS and OCBC.
picks.risks: A broad macro shock to Singapore banks (further bond yield spikes, NIM compression) would hit all three regardless of relative positioning; a results-day move historically averages 2.7%, so a surprise miss could still hurt.

picks.thesis: OCBC reports Nov 6 with net profit expected to fall sequentially to SGD1.9-2.0bn from SGD2.2bn on lower trading income, and the stock has already fallen the most among SG banks this month (-12.5% 1m, -13.5% from 52w high), reflecting the heaviest mark-to-market exposure from the bond yield surge. Weak guidance into the print plus ongoing STI tech/financial weakness (STI total returns -5.2% in October) support further downside into and after results.
picks.news: OCBC reports Nov 6 2026 with expected weaker q/q profit; Minichart (Oct 23) frames OCBC earnings as 'expected marginally weaker on lower trading income' within a sector under bond-yield pressure.
picks.risks: Banks often sell off into earnings and rally on 'less bad than feared' results; OCBC's -12.5% monthly decline may already fully discount the earnings miss, risking a relief rally post-print.

picks.thesis: Berkshire is acting as a defensive haven amid the tech-led volatility spike, up 2.5% on Nov 2-3 while the Nasdaq fell 2.9%, and is near its 52-week high with low volatility (14.9%) and a low beta (0.3). As investors rotate out of high-multiple AI names on spending-discipline concerns, Berkshire's diversified, value-oriented profile should continue to benefit on a relative basis.
picks.news: Berkshire rose 2.5% on Nov 2-3 2026 even as the broader Nasdaq tumbled 2.9% in its worst day in nearly five months amid the tech/AI selloff.
picks.risks: If the market selloff proves short-lived and risk appetite snaps back toward high-beta tech, Berkshire's relative outperformance could stall or reverse as money rotates back into growth names; the stock trades near its 52-week high with limited near-term analyst upside (-0.1% implied).

picks.thesis: The Nasdaq-100 just posted its worst single day in nearly five months on AI-capex concerns, with Apple and Amazon both disappointing and dragging the index down; QQQ is trading 6% below its 50-day moving average with elevated relative volume (1.39x), suggesting the selloff has momentum that could persist in the very near term as more mega-caps (including Nvidia on Nov 17) report.
picks.news: Nasdaq fell 2.9% (747.73 points) on Nov 2 2026, its worst day in nearly five months, driven by AAPL margin guidance disappointment and AMZN's earnings miss.
picks.risks: This is a short-term, event-driven trade; a quick reversal/dip-buying rally (common after single large down days) or a strong Nvidia-adjacent catalyst could reverse the move fast, and QQQ is still up 7.8% over the past year, so the broader trend remains intact.
